result:
The proposed answer of 1117 is incorrect. The formula for \(c_{n,k}\) fails for \(n=6, k=3\), where it gives \(2^{3-1}=4\) components.

The graph is the Cayley graph of \(\mathbb{F}_2^n\) with the weight-\(k\) vectors as generators. Its components are the cosets of the subgroup \(H\) spanned by those vectors, so \(c_{n,k}=2^n/|H|\).

For \(k<n\), take two weight-\(k\) vectors that share \(k-1\) positions. Their sum is a weight-2 vector \(e_i+e_j\). So \(H\) contains every even-weight vector.

- If \(k\) is odd, \(H\) also contains an odd-weight vector, so \(H\) is the whole space and \(c_{n,k}=1\).
- If \(k\) is even, every generator has even weight, so \(H\) is exactly the even-weight subspace and \(c_{n,k}=2\).

For \(k=n\), the only generator is the all-ones vector, so \(c_{n,n}=2^{n-1}\).

For \(n=6, k=3\), the correct value is therefore 1, not 4. The proposed formula \(2^{\gcd(k,n)-1}\) is wrong whenever \(\gcd>1\) and \(k<n\), so the sum of 1117 is wrong.

VERDICT: REJECT
